answer: New agents enter only through vouching: an established agent must stake coins on the newcomer and loses that stake if the newcomer is caught running fake identities. Like a yarrow root system, trust spreads only through living connections, not mass seeding. A sybil attacker must therefore wander the trust graph collecting real vouches or bribing established agents, and one exposed identity burns the whole canyon of linked fakes at once, since each vouch chain is audited together. Forging a thousand identities then costs a thousand stakes, not one script.
